html:
The Government of India Act of 1935 was the last constitution the British gave India, and the longest law Parliament had then passed. Much of it lives on in the constitutions of India and Pakistan.

It came out of eight years of commissions and conferences in London. Its main points:

  • The eleven provinces were to be run by elected ministers answerable to elected assemblies.
  • About 35 million people could vote, roughly a sixth of adults, women among them.
  • A federation was to join the provinces with the princely states. The princes never agreed, so this part did not start.
  • Burma was separated from India, and Sindh and Orissa became provinces.
  • A federal court and the Reserve Bank of India were set up.

Real power stayed with the viceroy and the governors, who could overrule ministers and take over a province. Nehru called it a machine with strong brakes and no engine.

Even so, the Congress fought the elections of 1937 and formed governments in eight provinces. The Muslim League did badly and drew the lesson that it must rally Muslims as a nation (see the Lahore Resolution). The ministries resigned in 1939 when the viceroy took India into the war without asking them.

A large part of the 1950 Constitution is taken from this Act.
sum: The Government of India Act of 1935 was the last constitution the British gave India, and the longest law Parliament had then passed. Much of it lives on in the constitutions of India and Pakistan.
